counterhypotheses.claim: A dedicated lightweight embedding encoder remains Pareto-superior because generative VLM visual features are not optimized for calibrated instance/layout similarity and open-set rejection.

No learned projection is needed; deterministic pooling and prototype statistics over raw Qwen features already provide sufficient familiarity geometry and projection training only adds drift/maintenance risk.
The vision tower dominates the cost or semantic decoder consultation is required so often that decoder bypass produces little real savings.
Desktop correctness depends on global layout/background/modal context often enough that ROI token reduction creates hidden failures exceeding its compute savings.
Periodic anchors are redundant when event capture and task-triggered active sensing are correct, so anchors waste compute without measurable resilience gain.
Full screenshot history or richer scene summaries preserve cross-region dependencies that action-grounded crops systematically lose.
Text/name anchors encode semantic category similarity rather than user-specific visual identity and will increase false familiarity for visually or semantically related entities.
Feature-space temporal distance is too sensitive to rendering/crop/resolution changes and too insensitive to small but task-critical text/state changes to be a reliable decode-control signal.

Model export/mmproj coupling or quantization changes can alter the representation enough that separating visual-feature compatibility from decoder behavior is not stable across actual deployed artifacts.
